svg.text: Tile-Centric Distributed Compiler Extension - ByteDance Seed - github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed - arXiv 2504.19442
L1 - Distributed Workloads + Targets (fine-grained compute-comm overlap - 1.09x to 44.97x vs NCCL/RCCL)
L2 - Tile-Centric Programming Model (MLSys 2025 TileLink philosophy - tile as unit of work)
Each tile independently computed / transferred / synced
Decouple comm tile size from compute tile size
Producer: P2P transfer + signal per tile ready
Consumer: wait tile signal then GEMM immediately
Break collectives into one-sided P2P + signals
No NCCL pre/post sync - tile-level coordination
Reorder comm + compute tiles for max overlap
L3 - triton_dist.language Primitives (OpenSHMEM + signal control - Python-level comm programming)
symm_at(ptr, rank) map local ptr to remote rank
Program comm + compute separately in Python
Minimal changes to original Triton compute code
consume_token(value, token) - data dep for MMA
Enables compiler pipelining between comm + compute
LL protocol: 8B atomic data+flag for inter-node
L4 - Dual-Path Compiler Stack (comm + compute merge at LLVM IR - single fused kernel)
Lower to LLVM IR + NVSHMEM/ROCSHMEM bitcode lib
Original Triton: TTIR - TTGIR - LLVM IR pipeline
Comm LLVM + compute LLVM linked into one module
Intra-node + inter-node P2P tasks run in parallel
Fuse multiple dist kernels into mega kernel
Qwen3 TP demo - intra-kernel profiler tooling
L5 - One-Sided Collective Patterns (push/pull modes - bandwidth vs latency tuning)
P2P tile push to symmetric buffers per rank
Signal consumer when each tile arrives
Push local shard + parallel local reduction
Two parallel parts sync via signals
L6 - Hardware Backends + Package Layout (python/triton_dist/ - kernels/ - test/ - docs/)
Three parallel tasks per rank: intra-node P2P + inter-node P2P + GEMM compute
Step 1: Host launches fused kernel - comm TBs + compute TBs on same device
Step 2: Producer TBs putmem_nbi_block tiles to symmetric remote buffers + set signal
Step 3: Consumer GEMM tile: token=wait(signal) - consume_token before load - MMA
Step 4: Tile swizzle aligns compute order with comm arrival - no global barrier wait
Step 5: Compiler lowers OpenSHMEM to NVSHMEM bitcode - merge w/ Triton LLVM - PTX
Result: comm latency hidden behind GEMM - beats NCCL operator-level overlap
2 nodes x 2 ranks: rank0/rank1 compute tile order differs to match comm arrival pattern
Only 2 extra primitives added to standard Triton GEMM: wait + consume_token per tile
First compiler with native fine-grained distributed overlap - Python not CUDA/C++
Design Position (distributed compiler extension - tile-level overlap replaces NCCL barrier model)
OpenSHMEM in Triton DSL + signal pipelining + tile swizzle = Python-level perf of hand-tuned C++ libs
Init: symm memory alloc - @triton_dist.jit kernel - host launch comm+compute threadblocks per rank
Loop: P2P tile push - signal - wait/consume_token - GEMM tile - swizzle order - LLVM merge - execute
